"You can choose the finish of images (photos or movies) by selecting a \"look\".
Creative look offers 6 preset looks. Each one is optimised with a different combination of colour tone, saturation, contrast, sharpness, brightness, and other image elements, so you can set up image processing with your ideal balance of these elements."
This look tones down some colours while enhancing the sky, greenery, and contrast. A good choice for natural landscapes showing the sea, sky, or mountains, or for other subjects against a blue sky.

This is the standard look for images. The settings, such as colour tones, colour depth (saturation) and contrast are adjusted to suit a wide range of subjects and scenes. This is useful when shooting snapshots of various subjects quickly and casually.
The saturation and contrast are increased for shooting striking images of colourful scenes and subjects such as flowers, greenery, blue skies, or ocean views.

"When using the ultra-wide lens (0.7x), you can select a priority. By selecting Prioritise image quality, you can capture dynamic high-quality images. If you select Prioritise correction for distortion, you can reduce visual distortion. This function is active when taking photos using the ultra-wide lens. After switching to the ultra-wide lens, you can configure the priority from MENU > Ultra-wide lens correction."

By creating a bright and cool colour finish, you can achieve a transparent expression. Recommended when you want to capture a clear skin tone or when you want to express the transparency of the sky or sea.
Reduces the contrast slightly and casts a slightly pink tone over the entire image. Recommended for evoking a dreamy atmosphere or emphasising the pink tones of sunsets.
This setting achieves cinematic gradations and colour expressions, allowing you to shoot with softer colour reproduction ideal for shooting portraits.

"Set the type of focusing frame when shooting with autofocus.
Wide: Focuses on subjects across the entire viewfinder. Centre: Focuses on subjects in the centre of the viewfinder. Focus and tracking: This setting is available only when the Focus mode is set to Continuous AF. When the device's shutter button is pressed and held halfway down, the camera tracks the subject within the selected autofocus area."
